questions.q: A block of mass $2$ kg is attached with two identical springs of spring constant $20Nm^{- 1}$ each. The block is placed on a frictionless surface and the ends of the springs are attached to rigid supports (see figure). When the mass is displaced from its equilibrium position, it executes a simple harmonic motion. The time period of oscillation is $\dfrac{π}{X}$ in SI unit. The value of $X$ is______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When the block is displaced by a distance& $x$, force acting on block due to both springs will be in the same direction. Therefore,

$F = - 2kx ⇒ a = - \dfrac{2k}{m}x,$

Comparing it with$a = - {ω}^{2}x$ , we get

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{2k}{m}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 20}{2}}$

$= \sqrt{20}rads^{- 1}$

Now,~$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{ω} = \dfrac{2\pi}{20} = \dfrac{π}{5}$

Hence, required value of~$X = 5$.

questions.q: When the displacement of a simple harmonic oscillator is one third of its amplitude, the ratio of total energy to the kinetic energy is $\dfrac{x}{8}$, where x =_________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The total energy of the harmonic oscillator is given by the formula

$E = \dfrac{1}{2}kA^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

where, $k$ is the force constant and $A$ is the amplitude.

The potential energy of the oscillator at the given displacement can be written as

\begin{cases}$U & = & $\d$dfrac{1}{2}k \left(\dfrac{A}{3}\right)2 \\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{kA^{2}}{2 \times 9}\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{E}{9}\end{cases}$

Hence, its kinetic energy is given by

$\begin{cases}KE \text{ and } = \text{ and } E - \dfrac{E}{9}\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{8E}{9}\end{cases}$

Thus, the required ratio is

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{E}{KE}& = & \dfrac{E}{8E9}\\ & = & \dfrac{9}{8}\end{cases}$

Hence, $x = 9$.

$

questions.q: The time period of simple harmonic motion of mass $M$ in the given figure is $\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{\alphaM}{5K}}$, where the value of $\alpha$ is _______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For series combination of the spring, equivalent spring constant is given by, $\dfrac{1}{keq} = \dfrac{1}{k1} + \dfrac{1}{k2}$.

Therefore, for combined system net spring constant ${k}_{eq} = \dfrac{2k \times k}{2k + k} + k = \dfrac{5k}{3}$

Angular frequency of oscillation \left(\omega\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{keq}{m}}$

$⇒ \left(\omega\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{5k}{3m}}$

Period of oscillation \left(τ\right) = \dfrac{2\pi}{ω} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{3m}{5k}}$

$= \pi\sqrt{\dfrac{12m}{5k}}$

Therefore, $\alpha = 12$.

questions.q: Two waves executing simple harmonic motion travelling in the same direction with same amplitude and frequency are superimposed. The resultant amplitude is equal to the $\sqrt{3}$ times of amplitude of individual motions. The phase difference between the two motions is _____ (degree)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When two& waves& of the& same frequency superimpose, the resultant amplitude is given by

${A}_{resultant} = \sqrt{{A}_{1}^{2} + {A}_{2}^{2} + 2{A}_{1}{A}_{2}cosϕ}$

$⇒ \sqrt{3}A = \sqrt{A^{2} + A^{2} + 2A^{2}cosϕ}$

$⇒ 3A^{2} = 2A^{2} + 2A^{2}cosϕ$

$⇒ cosϕ = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∴ ϕ = 60 °$

$∴$Phase difference $= 60$& degree

questions.q: A simple pendulum with length $100$ cm and bob of mass $250g$ is executing S.H.M of amplitude $10$ cm. The maximum tension in the string is found to be~$\dfrac{x}{40}N$. The value of $x$ is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the given figure we can see that&

$sin{θ}_{0} = \dfrac{A}{l} = \dfrac{10}{100} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

From conservation of energy~$\dfrac{mv^{2}}{2} = mgl ( 1 - cos{θ}_{0} )$

Maximum tension occurs at mean position

$T = mg + \dfrac{mv^{2}}{l} ⇒ T = mg + 2mg ( 1 - cos{θ}_{0} )$

Substituting the values,

$T = mg ( 1 + 2 ( 1 - \sqrt{1 - \sin^{2}{θ}_{0}} ) ⇒ T = mg ( 3 - 2\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{1}{100}} ) ⇒ T = 0 . 25 \times 9 . 8 ( 3 - 2 ( 1 - \dfrac{1}{200} ) ) ⇒ T = 0 . 25 \times 9 . 8 \times 1 . 01 = 2 . 4745N$

It is given that

~$T = \dfrac{x}{40} ⇒ x = 40 \times 2 . 4745 = 98 . 98 \approx 99$

questions.q: A mass $0 . 9kg$, attached to a horizontal spring, executes SHM with an amplitude ${A}_{1}$. When this mass passes through its mean position, then a smaller mass of $124g$ is placed over it and both masses move together with amplitude ${A}_{2}$. If the ratio $\dfrac{A1}{A2}$ is $\dfrac{α}{\alpha - 1}$, then the value of $\alpha$ will be _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At mean position, the velocity of the particle in S.H.M. is maximum, so kinetic energy is& $KE = \dfrac{1}{2}kA^{2}$, where,~$k$~is spring constant.

We also know that, kinetic energy is related to momentum as~$KE = \dfrac{p2}{2m}$.

Now, from both equations, we have~

$\dfrac{1}{2}kA^{2} = \dfrac{p2}{2m}$~ ~ ~(Here, momentum is conserved)

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{A1}{{A}_{2}}\right)2 = \dfrac{m2}{{m}_{1}} = \dfrac{1024}{900}$

$⇒ \dfrac{A1}{A2} = \dfrac{32}{30} = \dfrac{16}{15} = \dfrac{16}{16 - 1}$

$∴ \alpha = 16$

questions.q: A mass $m$ is suspended from a spring of negligible mass and the system oscillates with a frequency ${f}_{1} .$ The frequency of oscillations if a mass $9m$ is suspended from the same spring is ${f}_{2} .$ The value of $\dfrac{f1}{f2}$ is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Frequency of oscillation of a spring-block system is given by, $f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$

Therefore, for both cases, we can write

${f}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$ and

${f}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{9m}}$

Required ratio, $\dfrac{f1}{f2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{1}} = \dfrac{3}{1}$

questions.q: The general displacement of a simple harmonic oscillator is $x = Asin\omegat$. Let $T$ be its time period. The slope of its potential energy ($U$) − time ($t$) curve will be maximum when~$t = \dfrac{T}{β}$.~The value of~$\beta$& is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, displacement& $x = Asin \left(\omegat\right)

Now, potential energy of a simple harmonic oscillator is~$U = $\dfrac{1}{2}$m{ω}^{2}x^{2} = $\dfrac{1}{2}$m{ω}^{2}A^{2}\sin^{2} \left(\omegat\right)$,

So, slope of potential energy and time curve is~$\dfrac{dU}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{m{ω}^{3}A^{2}}{2}sin2\omegat$

Now,~\left(\dfrac{dU}{dt}\right)max$~will be maximum when~$sin2\omegat = 1$

~$⇒ 2\omegat = \dfrac{π}{2} ⇒ 2\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{T}\right)t = \dfrac{π}{2} ⇒ t = \dfrac{T}{8} ⇒ \beta = 8

$

questions.q: As per given figures, two springs of spring constants $K$ and $2K$ are connected to mass $m$. If the period of oscillation in figure (a) is $3s$, then the period of oscillation in figure (b) will be $\sqrt{x}s$. The value of $x$& is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In figure (a), the springs are connected in series. Therefore,

${K}_{eq} = \dfrac{{K}_{1}{K}_{2}}{{K}_{1} + {K}_{2}} = \dfrac{K \times 2K}{K + 2K} = \dfrac{2K}{3}$

Therefore, the time period

${T}_{a} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{Keq}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{\dfrac{2K}{3}}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{3m}{2K}}$

In~figure (b), the springs are connected in parallel. Therefore,

${K}_{eq} = {K}_{1} + {K}_{2} = 3K$

Therefore, the time period

${T}_{b} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{Keq}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{3K}}$

Now,

$\dfrac{Ta}{Tb} = \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{2}} ⇒ {T}_{b} = \dfrac{2}{3}{T}_{a} = \sqrt{2}s$

Hence,~$x = 2$

questions.q: A pendulum bob has a speed of $3ms^{- 1}$~at its lowest position. The pendulum is $50$ cm long. The speed of bob, when the length makes an angle of $60 °$ to the vertical will be  \left(g = 10ms^{- 2}\right)$~______~$ms^{- 1}$.$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Applying work energy theorem:

${w}_{g} + {w}_{T} = \Delta K$

$- mgl\left(1 - cos60 °\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}mu^{2}$

$v^{2} = u^{2} - 2gl \left(1 - cos60 °\right)$

$v^{2} = 9 - 2 \times10 \times0 . 5 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)

$v^{2} = 4$

$v = 2ms^{- 1}$

$

questions.q: A particle executes simple harmonic motion with an amplitude of $4$ cm. At the mean position, velocity of the particle is $10cms^{- 1}$. The distance of the particle from the mean position when its speed becomes $5cms^{- 1}$ is $\sqrt{\alpha}cm$, where \alpha =______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the velocity of the particle at the mean position is given by

$V = A\omega . . . \left(1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

$10 = 4 \times \omega⇒ \omega = $\dfrac{5}{2}$rads^{- 1}$

The formula to calculate the velocity of the particle at any instantaneous position $x$ can be expressed as

$v = \omega\sqrt{A^{2} - x^{2}} . . . \left(2\right)$

From equation (2), it follows that

$5 = \dfrac{5}{2}\sqrt{{4}^{2} - x^{2}} ⇒ x^{2} = 16 - 4 = 12 ⇒ x = \sqrt{12}cm$

Hence, $\alpha = 12$.

questions.q: A rectangular block of mass $5$ kg attached to a horizontal spiral spring executes simple harmonic motion of amplitude $1m$~and time period $3 . 14s$. The maximum force exerted by spring on block is ___ $N$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
By Newton's second law,

$F = m{a}_\max$.

The maximum acceleration for a SHM is given by~

${a}_\max = {ω}^{2}A . . . ( i )$

The time period is given by~

$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{ω} = 3 . 14s$

$⇒ \omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3 . 14} = 2rads^{- 1}$

Thus, the maximum acceleration from equation (i)

${a}_\max = 4 \times 1 = 4ms^{- 2}$

The maximum force is~

$F = 5kg \times 4ms^{- 2} = 20N$

questions.q: The amplitude of a particle executing SHM is $3$ cm. The displacement at which its kinetic energy will be $25 %$ more than the potential energy is: ______ $cm$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let $x$~be the displacement at which its kinetic energy will be~$25 %$~more than the potential energy.

Given here,~$A = 3cm$~and~$KE = PE + \dfrac{PE}{4}$

So,~$KE = \dfrac{5}{4}PE$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}m{ω}^{2}\left(A^{2} - x^{2}\right) = \dfrac{5}{4} \times \dfrac{1}{2}m{ω}^{2}x^{2}$

$⇒ A^{2} - x^{2} = \dfrac{5}{4}x^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{9x^{2}}{4} = A^{2}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{2}{3}A$

$∴ x = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 3cm$

$⇒ x = 2cm$

questions.q:
A particle of mass $0.50 \mathrm{~kg}$ executes simple harmonic motion under force $F=-50\left(\mathrm{Nm}^{-1}\right) x$. The time period of oscillation is $\frac{x}{35} \mathrm{~s}$. The value of $x$ is _______
(Given $\pi=\frac{22}{7}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{m}=0.5 \mathrm{~kg} \\ & \mathrm{~F}=-50(\mathrm{x}) \\ & \mathrm{ma}=(-50 \mathrm{x}) \\ & 0.5 \mathrm{a}=-50 \mathrm{x} \\ & \mathrm{a}=(-100 \mathrm{x}) \\ & \mathrm{W}^2=100 \Rightarrow(\mathrm{w}=10) \\ & \mathrm{T}=\frac{2 \pi}{10}=\left(\frac{\pi}{5}\right)=\frac{22}{7 \times 15}=\left(\frac{22}{35}\right) \\ & \frac{\pi}{35}=\frac{22}{35} \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=22\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Time period of a simple pendulum is $T$. The time taken to complete $\dfrac{5}{8}$ oscillations starting from mean position is $\dfrac{α}{12}T$. The value of $\alpha$ is~______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{5}{8}$th of oscillation $= \left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{8}\right)th$ of oscillation

$\pi + \theta = \omegat$

$\pi + \dfrac{π}{6} = \left(\dfrac{2\pi}{T}\right)t$

$\dfrac{7\pi}{6} = \left(\dfrac{2\pi}{T}\right)t$

$t = \dfrac{7T}{12}$

questions.q:
The velocity of a particle executing SHM varies with displacement ($x$) as $4v^{2} = 50 – x^{2}$. The time period of oscillations is~$\dfrac{x}{7}s$. The value of $x$ is ______.

[Take~$\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:

$4v^{2} = 50 - x^{2}$

$⇒ v = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{50 - x^{2}}$

Comparing with standard equation of SHM,~$v = \omega\sqrt{A^{2} - x^{2}}$, we get

$\omega = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Now,

$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{ω} = 4\pi = \dfrac{88}{7}$

Hence, required $x = 88$.

questions.q: A particle executes simple harmonic motion. Its amplitude is $8$ cm and time period is $6s$. The time it will take to travel from its position of maximum displacement to the point corresponding to half of its amplitude, is _____~$s$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here,& $A = 8cm$~and~$T = 6s$

The displacement equation in SHM, when amplitude~is halved is~$Acos\left(\dfrac{2\pit}{T}\right) = \dfrac{A}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{2\pit}{T} = \dfrac{π}{3}$

Time taken by the particle is~$t =$~$\dfrac{T}{6} = \dfrac{6}{6} = 1sec$.
